Rapid Emission-Economy Decoupling alongside the Urbanization of Chinese Counties.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: As China makes progress in air pollution control, the growing need for targeted pollution mitigation poses a great challenge for fine-scale emission tracking. However, the lack of up-to-date high-resolution emission data precludes a timely, spatially detailed assessment of emission distributions and their evolution with economic development. Here we derive summertime nitrogen oxides emissions from 2018 to 2024 for a total of 2,842 counties at different levels of urbanization in mainland China, based on satellite measurements and a fast, physics-based emission inversion method. The results show widespread declines in 84.1 ± 7.3% of counties. Among the 1,779 counties with available gross domestic product data, 76.7 ± 7.1% achieve absolute emission-economy decoupling (i.e., reduced emissions despite economic growth), and an additional 9.4 ± 3.9% exhibit relative decoupling (i.e., economic growth outpacing emissions growth). Relative emission reductions and emission-economy decoupling tend to be stronger in more urbanized counties, with the share of total national emissions moving toward less-urbanized, previously less-focused counties, particularly in the west. These results suggest structural progress toward greener development in Chinese counties along with an emerging need to shift attention toward less-urbanized locations.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Ultrafast NH4+ Capture by Prussian Blue Analogues Accelerated by the Hydrogen-Bond of Water.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Recovering ammonium (NH4+) from low-concentration wastewater represents a critical step toward sustainable nitrogen management. Although adsorption is widely regarded as the most promising strategy for NH4+ recovery from dilute streams, its practical application is often hampered by intrinsically slow kinetics and insufficient selectivity. Given the exceptional ion-sieving capability of Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), we hypothesized that water molecules confined within their framework channels create a dynamic hydrogen-bonded microenvironment that can modulate NH4+ transport. Inspired by this concept, we synthesized a series of Zn-based PBAs with controlled water contents via thermal treatment (denoted as Zn-PBAs-x, where x represents the treatment temperature). The sample with the highest water content (Zn-PBAs-60) exhibited an unprecedented NH4+ adsorption rate, with a pseudo-second-order rate constant (k2) of 4.35 g·mg-1·min-1. Integrated solid-state 1H magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (1H MAS NMR) and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed a "water-accelerated adsorption" mechanism: hydrogen-bonding interactions between framework nitrogen sites and water molecules significantly weaken the binding of NH4+ to the framework, thereby markedly accelerating NH4+ migration within the channels. This material achieved nearly 20-fold concentration of dilute NH4Cl within 3 min. This study provides new insights and strategic directions for the rapid enrichment and resource utilization of low-concentration ammonia nitrogen, contributing to the advancement of sustainable development pathways.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Decoupling Ion Selectivity and Transport via Dual-Scale Interlayer Nanochannels in Reduced Graphene Oxide Membranes for Lithium Separation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Selective separation of Li+ from coexisting Ni2+, Co2+, and Mn2+ is an important step in lithium recovery from spent lithium-ion batteries. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) membranes offer a promising platform for this separation through their ångström-scale interlayer nanochannels. However, the same narrow nanochannels hinder ion diffusion, inducing a severe permeability-selectivity trade-off. To decouple ion selectivity from transport, we report a nanoconfined sol-gel strategy for constructing a dual-scale interlayer architecture in rGO membranes. Intercalated between graphene oxide layers, aluminosilicate (AS) sols serve as cross-linkers and in situ vapor sources. During thermal aging, sol-gel condensation generates vapor that expands un-cross-linked galleries into transport highways, while cross-linked domains retain ion-selective confinement. The architecture is tunable across ion-selective interlayer spacing (dS, 7.1-8.3 Å) and expanded interlayer spacing (dE, 34-94 Å). Compared with conventional rGO membranes, the optimized dual-scale spacing membrane increases Li+ permeability 5.4-fold in mixed-ion solution while achieving high divalent-ion selectivity (Li+/Ni2+ = 246, Li+/Co2+ = 391, Li+/Mn2+ = 448). Molecular dynamics simulations attribute this selectivity to asymmetric energy barriers imposed on Li+ and divalent cations within the cross-linked spacing, while the expanded spacing facilitates low-resistance transport. This work shows how nanoconfined sol-gel chemistry can open a design space for fabricating high-performance ion recovery membranes.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Identification and Reaction Analysis of Antibiotic Transformation Products in an Urban River via Suspect and Nontarget Screening with a Self-Curated Library.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Antibiotics enter urban river basins mainly through sewage effluent. They undergo transformation during treatment and in river systems, generating transformation products (TPs) that may still have ecological effects. Yet, identifying these TPs by high-resolution mass spectrometry is hindered by the scarcity of reference standards and comprehensive MS/MS spectral libraries. To overcome this, we constructed a dedicated MS/MS library containing over 6,500 MS/MS spectra for 244 parent antibiotics and 362 TPs, thereby enabling rapid suspect screening through spectral matching. For novel TPs beyond library coverage, we integrated diagnostic fragment searching and seed-driven molecular networking to propagate annotations to structurally related unknowns. Applying this workflow to water, sediment, and effluent samples from an urban river system in Beijing, we identified 39 parent antibiotics and 158 TPs, of which 20 TPs are not previously documented in environmental samples. The major transformation reactions were cleavage, dealkylation, and hydrolysis, alongside compound-specific pathways like hemiacetal formation for erythromycin. These reactions differentially affect the environmental properties of antibiotics, and some reactions (e.g., dehydrogenation and dehydration) showed potential to enhance ecotoxicity. These results confirm that transformation substantially diversifies antibiotic signatures in urban aquatic environments and underscore the necessity of including TPs in environmental monitoring and risk assessment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Dissolved Organic Matter Charge Dynamics over Three Decades.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a crucial component of aquatic ecosystems, influencing pH, metal speciation, and the bioavailability of trace elements. The influence of DOM on water quality depends not only on its concentration but also on its chemical characteristics. To quantify the site density (SD) of organic acid functional groups, a key characteristic of DOM, this study utilized data from over 31,000 water samples collected from 110 watercourses between 1995 and 2024 by Swedish national monitoring programs. We found systematic dynamic trends in SD across Sweden. The analysis revealed an increase in SD from 1995 to 2003, followed by a decline from 2003 to 2010. Since 2010, SD has stabilized, although modest increases remain evident at many sites. Earlier trends were potentially governed by changes in DOM mobility associated with recovery from acid deposition, whereas more recent trends are likely linked to DOM source characteristics.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Plankton Size Structure Impacts PAH Bioaccumulation and Fate in Marine Pelagic Food Webs.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Plankton constitutes the primary entry point of contaminants into pelagic food webs, yet the role of plankton size structure in governing hydrocarbon fate remains poorly understood due to methodological limitations. Here, polycyclic aromatic (PAHs) and aliphatic (AHs) hydrocarbons were investigated across seven plankton size fractions (0.7 μm to >500 μm) collected in coastal waters of the northwestern Mediterranean Sea using a locally designed online sequential filtration system. Biochemical, isotopic, and molecular marker analyses were combined to characterize plankton composition, hydrocarbon sources, and PAH bioaccumulation patterns across size fractions. Molecular markers confirmed the transition from phytoplankton-dominated signatures in the smallest fractions to increasing zooplanktonic contributions in larger fractions. The 0.7-2.7 and 2.7-20 μm fractions, dominated by pico- and nanoplankton, accounted for the highest particulate organic carbon and hydrocarbon concentrations (3.0-3.4 μg g-1 dw for Σ26-PAHs) while zooplankton fractions (>60 μm) displayed lower values (0.09-0.69 μg g-1 dw). The passive uptake of low-molecular-weight (LMW) PAHs dominated across all size fractions but decreased with increasing plankton size. In contrast, high-molecular-weight (HMW) PAHs showed preferential accumulation in nanoplankton. These results demonstrate that plankton size structure and biomass dependent processes strongly influence PAH bioaccumulation and trophic transfer in marine pelagic food webs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Microplastics Promote Light-Driven Ferrihydrite Transformation by Altering the Balance between Interfacial Aggregation and Redox Processes.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Ferrihydrite (Fh) phototransformation regulates iron cycling and the mobility of nutrients and contaminants in aquatic and terrestrial environments. Microplastics (MPs) increasingly coexist with Fh, yet whether intact MP particles regulate Fh phototransformation through particle-scale interfacial effects remains unclear. We investigated how MPs (polystyrene (PS), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), and polylactic acid (PLA)) affect Fh transformation under simulated solar irradiation. Without MPs, irradiation produced predominantly hematite (Hm), with goethite (Gt) as a minor product, and 9.17% of Fh was transformed after 25 d. MPs increased the transformation without changing detectable products. MPs suppressed Fh reaggregation by shifting surface charge and disrupting Fh-Fh contacts, while enhancing irradiation-induced charge separation, surface Fe(III) reduction, Fe(III)/Fe(II) cycling, and Fe mobilization. The promoting effects outweighed aggregation inhibition, causing net promotion of Fh transformation. Notably, PLA hydrolysis and photo-oxidation lowered pH and released acidic, Fe-complexing photoproducts, amplifying Fe mobilization and the aqueous Fe pathway. Overall, the PLA > PVC > PS trend reflects coupled polymer chemistry, particle properties, intact-particle interactions, and irradiation susceptibility, with PLA-derived aqueous components providing an additional solution-phase contribution. These findings show that intact MPs and polymer-derived aqueous products jointly modify Fe mineral evolution, linking plastic aging to iron biogeochemistry in illuminated surface environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Paleoclimatic Legacies Help Explain Microbial Carbon Use Efficiency in Thawing Permafrost.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microbial decomposition in thawing permafrost mobilizes one of Earth's largest organic carbon reservoirs, releasing CO2 that amplifies global warming. This carbon-climate feedback depends strongly on microbial carbon use efficiency (CUE)─the ratio of biomass carbon synthesis to total carbon uptake, which governs the balance between carbon retention and respiratory loss. Although permafrost carbon and microbial communities developed thousands of years ago, how paleoclimatic legacies shape permafrost CUE remains unresolved. Here, by integrating 18O-H2O labeling with amplicon and metagenomic sequencing across a ∼1000-km transect on the Tibetan Plateau, we show that mid-Holocene paleoclimate outperforms contemporary drivers in explaining spatial variation in permafrost CUE. Sites with drier and more variable paleoclimates exhibited lower CUE (0.17 ± 0.07) than wetter and more climatically stable sites (0.43 ± 0.08). This lower CUE was linked to two pathways: geochemical constraints involving reduced nutrient availability and stronger phosphorus limitation, and microbial adaptations reflected in communities enriched in metabolically costly stress-tolerance and recalcitrant carbon-acquisition traits. Collectively, these paleoclimatic legacies accounted for 70% of CUE variation, underscoring the critical role of paleoclimate in shaping the vulnerability of permafrost carbon to respiratory loss upon thawing. Incorporating these millennial-scale legacies into Earth system models could improve projections of future permafrost carbon feedbacks.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: A Substitution Paradox in China's Plastics Sector: Climate Benefits of Degradable Materials Are Conditional on Energy-System Decarbonization.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Plastics are a rapidly growing source of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Degradable plastics are increasingly promoted to address plastic waste concerns, while biobased alternatives are also considered for their potential to reduce reliance on fossil feedstocks and lower life cycle GHG emissions. However, their system-level climate effects remain uncertain because existing assessments often focus on individual products or polymers and rarely account for realistic substitution feasibility, value-chain interactions, and end-of-life (EoL) constraints. Here, we integrated dynamic material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario modeling to evaluate the net GHG implications of substituting degradable plastics across China's plastics sector. The framework tracks five major conventional resins across 14 application sectors, links sector-specific substitution pathways with production-stage carbon intensities, and quantifies emission trajectories from 2025 to 2030, with long-term mitigation pathways explored to 2060. Technically feasible substitution increases cumulative life cycle GHG emissions by 7.1% relative to the conventional baseline because higher upstream production emissions outweigh potential EoL credits for recovered energy or displaced coproducts. Scenario analysis identifies a critical transition threshold: degradable plastics achieve net GHG reductions only when energy-system carbon intensity decreases by approximately 47% of the baseline level. The climate benefits of substitution are therefore conditional on coordinated energy-system decarbonization, production improvement, and waste-management development. Even under the optimistic pathway, 0.24 Gt CO2e of residual emissions remain in 2060, indicating the need for complementary mitigation measures.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Long-Term PM2.5 Exposure Promoted Vascular Calcification through XBP1s-Associated Osteogenic Switching and Inflammatory Crosstalk.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is a major environmental risk factor for cardiovascular disease, yet the mechanisms underlying long-term exposure-induced vascular calcification remain incompletely understood. Whether PM2.5 directly participates in mineral nucleation remains unclear. We found that PM2.5 accelerated the transformation of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) into crystalline hydroxyapatite (HAP) and may act as a heterogeneous nucleation interface under simulated physiological conditions. Mice were exposed to environmentally relevant PM2.5 concentrations (5 or 35 μg/m3) for 180 days using a whole-body inhalation system. Long-term PM2.5 exposure increased arterial stiffness and promoted vascular remodeling and calcification. Mechanistically, PM2.5 increased XBP1s expression in mouse aortic smooth muscle cells (MOVAS), promoting proliferative and osteogenic phenotypic switching. Genetic deletion of Xbp1 markedly attenuated PM2.5-induced MOVAS proliferation, migration, osteogenic transformation, and mineralization. In addition, PM2.5-stimulated MOVAS acquired a pro-inflammatory secretory phenotype that promoted macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization, whereas Xbp1 deficiency attenuated these effects. We also established a human iPSC-derived blood vessel organoid (BVO)-macrophage coculture system and found that macrophages substantially amplified PM2.5-induced osteogenic remodeling and calcification. Collectively, these findings revealed the involvement of both physicochemical mineralization and XBP1-associated osteogenic and inflammatory responses in PM2.5-induced vascular calcification, providing new insights into the mechanisms underlying PM2.5-associated vascular injury.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Spectroscopic Insights into Ion Pairing in Sulfate Electrolytes: Implications for Sorption in Aqueous Systems.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Ion pairing, including contact, solvent-shared, and solvent-separated ion pairs (CIPs, SIPs, and SSIPs, respectively), affects aqueous reaction chemistry, sorption, and precipitation processes. Accurate characterization of ion pairing in aqueous sulfate electrolytes is essential for understanding their thermodynamics and hydration structure, yet comprehensive quantification across aqueous and mixed-solvent systems remains limited. We combine Raman spectroscopy with dielectric spectroscopy, using waveguide-based setups (WR-62 and WR-28, applied for the first time) and a broadband probe station (10 MHz-50 GHz), to characterize ion pairing and solvent-solute interactions in monovalent cation sulfate salts in water and water/methanol solutions. Dielectric spectroscopy resolved SSIP and SIP fractions, with SSIPs dominating Li2SO4 and Na2SO4. Raman spectroscopy quantified CIPs (K2SO4 > Na2SO4 ≈ Li2SO4), consistent with cation hydration and polarizability. Methanol increased SIP and CIP concentrations. Ion association stability constants and mean activity coefficients were calculated with Archer's form of the Pitzer model, incorporating short-range binary and ternary ion-ion interactions. This approach predicts mean activity coefficients at elevated ionic strengths without double-counting ion-pairing contributions, enabling determination of stability constants and aqueous speciation. Resolving ion-pair speciation is important for accurate thermodynamic models of sulfate-bearing waters relevant to membrane separations and resource recovery.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: A Scenario-Based Probabilistic First-Tier Screening of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean-Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan-Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Gradient-Charge Oxygen Vacancy Pairs Enable Synergistic Activation of O2 and H2O for Low-Temperature CH3CN Emission Control.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti-OVR-Cu-OVP-Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti-OVR-Cu-OVP-Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Nanoconfinement Controls Hydrogen Transport in Shales.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) in sedimentary formations requires understanding how hydrogen migrates, persists, and is released under nanoscale confinement in fine-grained rocks that may act as reservoirs or caprocks. Here, we combine in situ small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with molecular dynamics simulations to examine how wetting state controls hydrogen reversibility and postcycling pore occupancy in shale nanopores. SANS-derived pore-size distributions reveal a clear hierarchy: dry shale exhibits near-complete reversibility, decane-saturated shale shows partial recovery, and water-saturated shale displays minimal recovery, with persistent postcycling occupancy concentrated in pores <2 nm. Molecular simulations support a mechanistic interpretation in which this hierarchy arises from coupled nanoscale effects, including cavity-formation penalties, confinement-induced stress anisotropy, and fluid-specific interfacial free-energy barriers at mineral and organic surfaces. Water-saturated nanopores are associated with strong thermodynamic and mechanical constraints consistent with reduced hydrogen reversibility, whereas these constraints are substantially weaker in dry pores and intermediate in decane-filled pores. Together, the experimental and molecular simulation results provide a framework linking nanoscale fluid-rock interactions to hydrogen hysteresis and retention, with implications for subsurface hydrogen recoverability and containment in underground storage systems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Strategies for Eliminating Heavy Air Pollution in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei Region: Insights from Joint Practices during the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10-4 and 1 × 10-5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Evaluating Pollution Prevention Effectiveness for Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences Methods.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada's National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993-2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001-2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Impacts of Biological Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net "sink" to a net "source" of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink-source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Aldehyde-philic Portal Engineering of γ-Cyclodextrin MOF for Synergistic Capture of Toluene and Formaldehyde in Humid Atmospheric Environments.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Efficient removal of multicomponent volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from real environments remains challenging, particularly under humidity. This study introduces an "aldehyde-philic portal modification" strategy that precisely anchors dopamine (DA) at γ-cyclodextrin-based metal-organic framework (γ-CD-MOF) outer rim via H-bonding to construct oligomeric polydopamine (o-PDA) structures. This pore design partitions the cyclodextrin cavity into an aldehyde-philic outer rim and arene-philic interior for efficient synergistic capture of formaldehyde and toluene in humidity. Exposed pyrrolic N sites on o-PDA enable γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 to preferentially bind CH2O, which then act as new sites to enhance subsequent C7H8 capture via CH-π interactions while hindering H2O binding to peripheral hydroxyls and preventing large-sized water clusters from blocking cavity openings. Furthermore, the hydrophobic inner cavity exhibits strong π-π conjugation with C7H8, facilitating its diffusion and establishing an "outer capture-inner fixation" pathway, significantly enhancing toluene capacity. At ∼40% relative humidity, the toluene working capacity of γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 in the multicomponent system increased by 106% over the single-component system, while the formaldehyde capacity remained unchanged. Consequently, the total working capacity of toluene and formaldehyde reached twice the sum of their single-component adsorption capacities, demonstrating marked synergistic coadsorption. This work provides a feasible approach for controlling multicomponent VOCs in complex humid atmospheric environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Turning Abandoned Mines into Carbon Sinks: Laboratory Demonstration of CO2 Hydrate Sequestration in Cold-Region Goafs under Permafrost Conditions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110-130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15-277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m-3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21-16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%-90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Near-Real-Time Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol Optical Depth in China.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China's clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day-night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: TP-Agent: An Auditable LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Engineering High-Entropy Interfaces in a Single-Metal Cu System to Drive Concerted Nonradical Catalysis and Pollutant Sequestration.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nonradical direct electron transfer (DET) can make advanced oxidation less vulnerable to radical scavenging in complex waters, but requires catalysts with efficient charge transport, stability, and practical synthesis. High-entropy materials provide diverse local environments, yet their multimetal compositions and prolonged heat treatment limit implementation. We combined chemically induced self-internal heating (SIH) with chloride-induced interfacial reconstruction to prepare a single-metal Cu system with high-density grain boundaries (SM-HDGB). SIH formed a Cu-carbon precursor in 3.5 s through an internal pulse above 1200 °C. HCl treatment generated intergrown Cu, Cu2O, CuCl, and Cu2Cl(OH)3 domains spaced 2-10 nm apart, creating phase, oxidation-state, and coordination diversity described as empirical interfacial chemical-state entropy. SM-HDGB completely removed tetracycline within 10 min and increased the apparent rate constant 9.88-fold over the precursor, with little response to 10 mM coexisting anions. Electron paramagnetic resonance, scavenging, filtration, electrochemical, and in situ spectroscopic evidence supported predominantly surface-confined, catalyst-mediated DET. In packed-bed operation, SM-HDGB maintained more than 80% COD removal across four regeneration cycles (approximately 130 h), retained pollutant-derived organic products, and produced near-neutral effluent compatible with Chlorella growth. Laboratory-scale screening estimated at least 96.3% lower synthesis energy demand than conventional routes. Chemical-state-diverse single-metal interfaces can therefore couple rapid peroxydisulfate activation with stable continuous-flow treatment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Solar-Driven Cu(II)-Cu(III) Redox Cycle on Decahedral BiVO4 for Scalable Water Purification.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Conventional Fenton-like reactions rely on external oxidants to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS, e.g., high-valent metal-oxo species (HVMS)), a practice that is inherently unsustainable for water purification. Here, we propose a solar-driven Cu(II)-Cu(III) redox cycle that differs from the traditional view that HVMS generation originates from peroxide-mediated pathways. By tuning the anisotropic built-in field of decahedral BiVO4, photogenerated holes accumulate selectively on its {110} family, enabling hole-driven hydrated Cu(II) oxidation instead of water. This facilitates an oxygen atom transfer (OAT) from adjacent Bi-OH sites to the H-bonded Cu(II) center, stabilizing the Cu(III)-oxo center by forming the Bi-O-Cu(III)-O structure (Cu(III)). Meanwhile, electron-driven dissolved oxygen reduction maintains charge balance. The photosynthetic Cu(III) mediates antibiotic degradation with a rate constant of 0.174 min-1, representing a ∼16-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant compared to traditional photocatalysis. Crucially, the solar BiVO4 sheet/Cu(II) system sustains consistent up to ∼85% moxifloxacin degradation efficiency in each cycle over 35 days. No total Cu was detected in the effluent of cycling experiments after pH adjustment (∼7.5). These findings provide a new solution to the long-standing challenge of achieving peroxide-free HVMS synthesis and scalable water purification.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Organoid-Based Strategy for Exploration of Cancer-Related Early Signatures of Low-Dose Methylmercury Exposure.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Methylmercury (MeHg) compounds are classified as Group 2B agents, possibly carcinogenic to humans by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), and as Group C possible human carcinogens by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), but the carcinogenic implications of environmentally relevant low-dose exposure remain unclear. Here, we established a population-informed organoid-based strategy to explore the potential of low-dose MeHg exposure leading to cancer incidence. A National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)-based analysis revealed nonlinear associations of blood MeHg with overall cancer history with increased predicted cancer probability around 5.39 μg/L for MeHg. Liver organoid experiments showed that low-dose MeHg did not cause overt short-term cytotoxicity but induced DNA damage and stress-response signatures after prolonged exposure. Transcriptomic analysis further linked low-dose MeHg exposure to cancer-related stress pathways, including reactive oxygen species (ROS) associated chemical carcinogenesis, p53 signaling, DNA repair, mitochondrial stress, and cell-cycle regulation. These results indicate that low-dose MeHg exposure could trigger early biological responses related to cancer-associated processes before apparent cytotoxicity occurs. This study supports organoid models as a human-relevant strategy for linking population exposure signals with tissue-level toxicological evidence in MeHg research and provides a potentially adaptable framework for evaluating subtle health effects of low-dose environmental pollutants.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Investigating the Relationships between the Structure and Cytotoxicity of Ionic Liquids in the Context of Cell Lines Being Affected.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Current quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models of ionic liquid (IL) cytotoxicity are generally developed for specific biological systems and cannot be assumed to transfer across cell types. Here, we evaluated 81 ILs spanning eight cationic head groups and 13 anions in HEK293T, CaCo-2, and DF-1 cell lines. The alkyl side chain length was the dominant structural determinant within homologous series, whereas cation, anion, and functionalization effects were most evident among ILs with shorter alkyl side chains. Mechanistic assays with 1-alkyl-3-methylimidazolium chlorides revealed distinct 24-h cellular response profiles in HEK293T and DF-1 cells, including different patterns of membrane permeabilization, apoptosis, and mitochondrial membrane potential changes. Descriptor-cytotoxicity correlations were strong within homologous imidazolium series but were less transferable across other structural comparisons. These results show that structure-based models can be informative within a defined chemical and cellular domain, but the cell type and cytotoxic response must be considered when extrapolating the IL cytotoxicity and assessing the safety of ILs proposed as greener process media.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Zeolite-Regulated Electron-Rich Cu-O-Ce Sites for Efficient Denitrification against Alkali/Heavy Metal Poisoning.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Enhancing the wide-temperature-window deNOx activity of catalysts under alkali/heavy metal poisoning conditions remains a pivotal challenge in the field of environmental catalysis. To tackle this issue, we designed a novel CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst using an acid-rich zeolite-modulated electron-enriched metal site strategy. This strategy enables the contact between strong acid sites and Cu-O-Ce active sites, simultaneously regulating the efficient NH3-SCR temperature window and enhancing K/Pb poisoning resistance. Compared to CuCeOx, the engineered acid-rich interface significantly facilitates electron transfer from ZSM-5 to CuCeOx, generating electron-rich Cu-O-Ce active sites. These sites not only serve as adjacent adsorption and activation centers for reactants but also inhibit NH3 oxidation, and CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst achieves >90% deNOx efficiency over a wide temperature range of 180-410 °C (T90 = 180-410 °C). K deactivates the catalyst mainly by reducing surface acidity and promoting the accumulation of less-reactive nitrate species, while Pb primarily suppresses Ce4+ → Ce3+ reduction via inducing Cu2+ → Cu+ conversion and occupying CeO2 oxygen vacancies. Notably, the poisoned CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst still retains satisfactory deNOx performance, with the T90 = 230-380 °C. This work not only provides novel mechanistic insights into the deactivation pathways of NH3-SCR catalysts by alkali and heavy metal ions but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of high-performance, poisoning-tolerant NH3-SCR catalysts tailored for complex flue gas environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Partition-Buffered Leaching of 6PPD-Quinone from Tire Wear Particles.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: 6PPD-quinone (6PPDQ; N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine-quinone) forms on tire-derived solid surfaces, including those of intact tires and environmentally dispersed tire wear particles (TWPs), yet its leaching kinetics remain insufficiently characterized for confident use in watershed and coastal fate-and-transport models. Here, we conducted time-resolved saturated column leaching experiments to quantify 6PPDQ leaching from lab-generated TWPs and to derive a physically based parametrization. Across hour-to-month observation windows, TWPs exhibited sustained, nearly linear 6PPDQ release (α ≈ 1) and weak particle-size scaling of the characteristic time scale, inconsistent with whole-particle Fickian diffusion. We tested a mechanistic hypothesis that strong TWP-water partitioning buffers aqueous concentrations and limits 6PPDQ mass export. Using a well-mixed column reactor (WMCR) representation, we estimated the TWP-water partition coefficient Ksw for the columns. The regression yielded log10 Ksw = 4.37 ± 0.22. Building on this mechanistic interpretation, we derived a Newtonian first-order leaching term suitable for hydrologic and coastal modeling. A two-compartment formulation further indicated that the TWP concentration, cTWP, strongly controls the apparent fraction of 6PPDQ released to the dissolved phase. These findings may help explain variability across prior leaching studies while bridging inconsistencies between experimental and field measurements.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Missed Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber's Carbon Storage Potential.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4-2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber's storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8-12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Electron Transfer Pathways Stretching from the Extracellular to Intracellular Membrane in Biohybrids Enable Enhanced CO2 Upcycling to Malate.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) empowers one-step conversion of CO2 to long-chain chemicals under mild conditions, enabling sustainable biomanufacturing and achievement of a circular carbon economy. Although the construction of biohybrids has been explored to enhance the inherently low efficiency of MES, whether the binding modes between nanomaterials and microorganisms dictating CO2 conversion efficiency remain elusive. To address this query, we constructed biohybrids with three distinct integration modes (namely, internalization, outer membrane-contact, and transenvelope) between nanomaterials and Shewanella, enabling to proceed CO2-to-malate conversion. Upon MES-driven CO2-to-malate conversion, the transenvelope biohybrid constituted by polydopamine and Shewanella achieved a marked gram-scale malate titer of 19.14 mmol/L, as a result of the distinctive transenvelope capacity of polydopamine stretching from the extracellular to the intracellular membrane. This transenvelope capacity imparts extended electron transfer pathways spanning from the cytoplasmic membrane to the extracellular space, significantly reducing interfacial barriers at the electrode-microorganism interface and greatly promoting NADH and ATP synthesis for malate synthesis, which can enhance NADH synthesis. This work proposes the construction of a transenvelope biohybrid to optimize microbial metabolism, offering an alternative for the efficient valorization of CO2 to carbon-negative long-chain chemicals.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Organophosphate Flame Retardants Induce Neurodegenerative Pathologies by Paralyzing HSP90AB1 Chaperone Function: A Multi-Scale Computational and Biophysical Study.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: This study integrated computational toxicology with biophysical and cellular validation to investigate the neurotoxic potential of 10 flame-retardant-related compounds. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted blood-brain barrier probabilities of 0.989 for bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and 0.444 for diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), interpreted as screening predictions. Network topology analysis identified HSP90AB1 as a shared candidate hub target linking organophosphate flame retardants to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated a stable HSP90AB1 backbone in the DPHP complex (root-mean-square deviation ∼0.18 nm). Surface plasmon resonance measured an equilibrium dissociation constant of 1.49 μM. DPHP induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in neuronal cells; the half-maximal inhibitory concentration was not determined within the tested range. HSP90AB1 overexpression mitigated DPHP-induced reactive oxygen species production and transcriptional upregulation of pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory genes. Single-cell virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory processes; Parkinson's disease-related enrichment remained exploratory after multiple-testing correction. Together, the computational, biophysical, and cellular findings support HSP90AB1 as a candidate target of environmental neurotoxicity and motivate further investigation of DPHP.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Multitechnique Characterization of Dissolved Organic Matter from Naturally Acidic and Circumneutral Waters Reveals Molecular Controls on Organic Nitrogen Speciation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The molecular characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) vary across seasons, catchments, and land uses, highlighting the need for generalized structure-function relationships that can predict intrinsic DOM bioavailability. This study characterized DOM from naturally acidic (pH 4.3-5.7) and circumneutral (pH 6.8-8.3) freshwaters over two seasons: winter-spring (WS) and summer-autumn (SA) using multiple characterization techniques (optical, fluorescence, targeted LC-MS/MS, 13C NMR, and FTIR). DOM from acidic environments was higher in aromaticity, more humic-like, with a higher C:N ratio but with a greater percentage of nitrogen in the form of amino acids (i.e., DCAA-N%). Seasonality was only observed for neutral samples, with differences between WS and SA dominated by a decrease in nominal molecular weight (MWn) in SA, likely driven by photochemical disaggregation. FTIR analysis indicates that neutral DOM has a higher amide group abundance than acidic DOM despite the lower DCAA-N%, suggesting the dominance of nonproteinaceous amide-N. Very strong dependencies were observed for dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) speciation against aromaticity (SUVA254) and an FTIR-derived ratio of deprotonated carboxylic:aromatic groups, describing the relative hydrophilicity-hydrophobicity of the DOM environment. These parameters largely explain the DCAA distribution and may provide a more generalized way of characterizing DOM that could be applied across different aquatic ecosystems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Toward Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Tire-Derived Organic Pollutants across Urban Land Uses: Associations with Traffic Exposure.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Tire-derived organic pollutants (TDOPs), particularly N-(1,3-dimethylbutyl)-N'-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD) and its transformation product 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), are increasingly recognized as emerging urban contaminants. However, their distribution and potential drivers in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment remain poorly characterized. In this study, 19 TDOPs were quantified in 28 urban soil samples representing four land-use types in Metro Detroit, Michigan, United States. TDOPs were widely detected in all soil samples, and 16 compounds exhibited detection frequencies ≥75%. Very low 6PPD/6PPD-Q ratios and the relative enrichment of N,N'-diphenyl-p-phenylenediamine (DPPD) over 6PPD suggest substantial environmental transformation of 6PPD. No statistically significant differences in the concentrations of TDOPs among land-use types or associations with measured soil properties were detected. In contrast, 6PPD exhibited a strong positive association with traffic-derived exposure metrics. The maximum Spearman rank correlation coefficient was observed for the commercial traffic exposure metric at a distance-decay parameter of 800 m (ρ = 0.76), and the association remained significant after optimization-adjusted permutation testing (pperm = 0.00030) and false discovery rate correction (q = 0.0048). This study demonstrates the widespread occurrence of TDOPs in urban soils beyond the immediate roadside environment and identifies modeled traffic exposure as an important correlate of soil 6PPD concentrations.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Contrasting Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes over the Tibetan Plateau.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Particle-bound semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs) reaching high-mountain regions are commonly interpreted in terms of temperature-driven gas-particle partitioning and precipitation scavenging. To investigate these competing dynamics, we report year-round, synchronous measurements of particle-bound organophosphate esters (OPEs) in PM2.5 at two contrasting Tibetan Plateau sites: a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). ΣOPEs averaged 111 ± 125 pg m-3 at QOMS and 20 ± 17 pg m-3 at NAMORS, exhibiting a counterintuitive warm-season maximum. This warm-season peak coincided with a 72-91% decline in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosols, indicating that trans-Himalayan transport sustains substantial particle-bound OPE inputs during the monsoon despite intense wet deposition. Furthermore, chlorinated congeners with stronger particle association (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated at both sites (TCEP/TCPP = 0.09-0.46). This contrasts with the highly volatile TCEP-dominated profiles reported for Arctic aerosols. Such a difference is consistent with an orographic modulation favoring particulate-phase retention during the shorter trans-Himalayan ascent. However, the lack of simultaneous gas-phase data and potential differences in regional emission histories must also be acknowledged. Back-trajectory clustering and principal component analysis both point to South Asian source regions as the principal control at QOMS. Consequently, correlations of OPEs with temperature and precipitation are better read as proxies for monsoon transport intensity than as evidence of local thermodynamic partitioning. Continued transboundary input suggests that particle-bound OPEs may contribute to deposition and subsequent accumulation in the alpine cryosphere, highlighting the urgent need to incorporate transboundary transport pathways into regional contaminant assessments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Emerging Hexafluoropropylene Oxide Trimer Acid Potently Targets Farnesoid X Receptor and Triggers Hepatic Cholestasis.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) hepatotoxicity is a critical global health threat, and disrupted bile acid metabolism is considered a key driver of PFAS-triggered liver injury, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Herein, we explored the hepatotoxic mechanisms of emerging hexafluoropropylene oxide trimer acid (HFPO-TA) and dimer acid (HFPO-DA) via farnesoid X receptor (FXR), assessed their health risks, and further compared their effects against perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). In rat, HFPO-TA exerted more potent hepatotoxicity than PFOA and HFPO-DA, triggering typical cholestasis through impaired biliary excretion and altered bile acid pool. Mechanistically, all three PFASs promoted the intracellular bile acid accumulation by inhibiting FXR transcriptional activity, with potent HFPO-TA > PFOA > HFPO-DA. Accordingly, HFPO-TA, HFPO-DA, and PFOA can directly bind to FXR though entering the ligand-binding domain via hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions to stabilize an antagonizing conformation. Notably, HFPO-TA bound FXR with 3.25-fold higher affinity than endogenous chenodeoxycholic acid and 50-fold higher affinity than PFOA, accompanied by elevated receptor-bound concentrations (RBCs). RBC-based risk assessment revealed moderate risk in 28.3% of HFPO-TA-exposed residents. Overall, HFPO-TA directly binds to FXR to induce hepatic cholestasis; such FXR-mediated cholestasis poses notable health risks and warrants broad vigilance toward PFAS liver hazards.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Biomass Hydrothermal Reduction Enables Direct Copper Recovery from Wastewater.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Recovering copper (Cu) from strongly acidic copper wastewater (SACW) is essential for resource sustainability and environmental preservation, but conventional technologies bear high economic costs and generate secondary pollution. Here, we demonstrate a biomass waste-mediated hydrothermal reduction process that simultaneously removes and recovers Cu as metallic Cu from SACW. The process operates under mild conditions (180 °C, 7 h) and achieves over 99% removal of Cu(II) across a wide concentration range, directly reducing Cu(II) to metallic Cu(0) without incorporation into hydrochar. Notably, the liquid products from biomass hydrothermal treatment, particularly 2-furoic acid, served as electron donors for Cu(II) reduction, with its C2/C3 atoms potentially providing electron transfer channels that drive the stepwise reduction of Cu(II) to Cu(0). In a 5 L pilot test with two types of industrial wastewater, the technology achieved >99% Cu(II) removal (residual <0.5 mg/L) and recovered metallic Cu with a purity of 99.9% after simple calcination. Life-cycle assessment and technoeconomic analysis highlight superior economic and environmental benefits when treating high-concentration copper-containing wastewater, establishing a sustainable, generalized hydrothermal reduction platform for efficient Cu recovery from industrial wastewaters. This work establishes a chemistry-driven paradigm for sustainable wastewater treatment, enabling efficient circular recovery of high-value resources from acidic metal-containing wastewaters.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Non-Targeted Characterization and Hazard-Based Prioritization of Disinfection Byproducts and Co-Contaminants in U.S. Drinking Water Distribution Systems.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Higher-carbon (>C2) disinfection byproducts (DBPs) remain poorly characterized in drinking water distribution systems (DWDSs) despite evidence that they may contribute substantially to drinking water toxicity. Here, we applied liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry and non-targeted analysis to characterize >C2 DBPs and co-contaminants across 12 U.S. DWDSs spanning a range of pre-oxidation and disinfection strategies. For each DWDS, we analyzed finished drinking water and distribution system samples collected at locations representing short, medium, and long distances from the treatment plant. We identified multiple classes of >C2 DBPs, including non-halogenated and halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids, halohydroxybenzaldehydes, halonitrophenols, (halo)phenylacetamides, (halo)fumaric acids, and several emerging nitrogenous DBPs. In addition, we also detected various co-contaminants such as pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals. DBPs and co-contaminants exhibited system-specific occurrence and spatial patterns, and non-halogenated hydroxybenzoic acids emerged as an overlooked and widespread class of DBPs. To support prioritization efforts, hazard data from EPA's Hazard Comparison Module was used to develop and implement hazard-weighted prioritization metrics. This approach identified (halo)hydroxybenzoic acids, halonitrophenols, DEET, triazine herbicides, and 2-hydroxyquinoline as high-priority contaminants, indicating that both emerging DBPs and co-contaminants may contribute to mixture-level hazards in distributed drinking water. Overall, this work expands the known >C2 DBP landscape and provides a framework for prioritizing drinking water contaminants detected by non-targeted analysis.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Sulfur-Vacancy-Enabled Dual-Site MoS2 Enhances H* Utilization for Mo-H-Mediated Deep Dechlorination.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrochemical dechlorination using molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) offers a cost-effective solution for treating chlorinated organic contaminants, yet its catalytic potential remains limited by the unclear roles of Mo and S sites in mediating hydrogen utilization and C-Cl bond cleavage. Herein, we engineer sulfur-vacancy-rich MoS2 (Sv-MoS2) electrodes to expose coordinatively unsaturated Mo sites and enable an efficient Mo-H*-mediated dechlorination pathway. Using florfenicol as a model chlorinated antibiotic, Sv-MoS2 achieved near-complete dechlorination with ∼15-fold faster kinetics than pristine MoS2, reaching a rate constant of 9.26 h-1 at low energy consumption (0.0083 kWh g-1). Mechanistic analyses combining CV, EPR, in situ Raman spectroscopy, kinetic isotope effects, and DFT calculations reveal a dual-site H* utilization mechanism: S sites primarily generate H*, while vacancy-exposed Mo sites stabilize Mo-H* species that selectively drive C-Cl bond cleavage. In contrast, pristine MoS2 follows a direct electron transfer-dominated pathway and shows limited deep dechlorination. The Mo-H*-mediated pathway on Sv-MoS2 substantially lowers the energy barriers for sequential C-Cl cleavage while promoting productive H* utilization over H2 formation. The Sv-MoS2 electrode further exhibits robust performance under variable pH, natural organic matter, coexisting anions, and repeated cycling. This work clarifies Mo/S site synergy in MoS2 electrocatalysts and establishes a dual-site design framework for efficient, selective, and sustainable electrochemical hydrodechlorination.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Microplastics Rapidly Sink and Beach in a Whole-Lake Experiment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Although advances in oceanographic and limnological modeling have increased our understanding of microplastic transport and persistence, we require more knowledge to effectively protect biodiversity. We initiated a whole-lake experiment (the pELAstic project) to measure the real-world fate and transport of microplastics. We added microplastics to a boreal lake, simulating stormwater input, at loading concentrations predicted to achieve environmentally relevant concentrations. Here, we introduce our experiment and describe the particle budget from the first microplastic addition. We observed rapid transport of microplastics to different ecosystem compartments. Transport patterns could not be fully explained by initial particle size and density, highlighting how natural processes modify plastic fate in real-world systems. Microplastic fragments rapidly redistributed─exiting the water column and settling on the bottom and shorelines. A particle budget across the water column, bottom sediments, and beaches accounted for 77% of the polyethylene, 48% polystyrene, and >100% polyethylene terephthalate. "Missing" plastic was likely in the nearshore littoral. Our observations suggest that if we prevent further inputs to aquatic ecosystems, microplastics will quickly disappear from the water column─washing up on shorelines and settling on the bottom. Thus, understanding rates of microplastic deposition and burial is critical to forecast the legacy of microplastic pollution.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Emerging CRISPR Technologies for Environmental Protection: From Genetic Engineering and Biosensing to Environmental Deployment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Since its discovery, Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR) has revolutionized biomedical science and engineering with its ability to recognize and edit gene sequences with high specificity and precision. Despite the growing interest in using these capabilities to address environmental and sustainability challenges, the broader potential of CRISPR in environmental systems remains unexplored relative to its biomedical applications. Here, we provide a critical perspective on the emerging use of CRISPR for pollution management, ecological conservation, and environmental monitoring. Rather than viewing CRISPR solely as a gene-editing or biosensing technology, we consider both capabilities together to examine how advances in CRISPR engineering can translate into practical environmental solutions. We highlight the fundamental principles behind CRISPR-based editing and sensing and evaluate the challenges that constrain their transition from proof-of-concept experiments to field deployment, including off-target effects, delivery methods, ecological risks, and low sensitivity. Addressing these hurdles requires a multifaceted approach that integrates emerging technologies such as reversible CRISPR technology, amplification and cascade reactions, and machine learning, with strict regulatory oversight and rigorous risk assessments. This perspective identifies critical strengths, weaknesses, and research priorities for advancing CRISPR from laboratory technology toward robust tools for environmental applications.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Technological Substitution in Pesticide Application Reduces Occupational Risk but Fails to Mitigate Dietary Residue Burden: Field Evidence from UAV versus Manual Spraying in Paddy Rice.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: UAV spraying has been widely promoted as superior to manual application in Asian rice production, yet its combined implications for food safety and occupational exposure have never been evaluated within a single integrated framework. Here, we report a full-season field trial comparing UAV and manual imidacloprid (IMI) application in paddy rice, simultaneously tracking grain residue dynamics and occupational exposure in 29 applicators through to harvest. Grain IMI concentrations at harvest were comparable between regimes (86-115 μg/kg) and exceeded the EU maximum residue limit (MRL, 10 μg/kg) in both groups. More critically, on an LC-HRMS-derived relative-concentration basis, parent IMI accounted for 30.4% of the detected IMI-related profile in grain, whereas transformation products collectively accounted for 69.6%. Among these, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid was the single highest-abundance compound, surpassing parent IMI itself, yet none of the detected transformation products are included in China's residue definition for imidacloprid in plant-derived foods. Regarding occupational exposure, urinary IMI rose approximately 9-fold from pre-exposure baseline in UAV operators compared with 17-fold in manual applicators. Manual application also induced markedly greater lipid peroxidation stress, with median baseline-normalized MDA fold changes of approximately 3.8- and 2.6-fold in the manual and UAV groups, respectively (p = 0.001). These findings establish that application technology substitution effectively reduces occupational exposure risk but confers no advantage at the food safety end point. Current parent-compound-centered residue surveillance frameworks systematically underestimate the true IMI-related burden in harvested grain, and expansion of regulatory monitoring beyond the parent compound is warranted.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Abnormal Event Monitoring of Drainage Pipelines Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Vibration Sensing.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Urban drainage networks are critical infrastructure for modern cities, yet their complex and concealed nature makes real-time monitoring of abnormal events a persistent challenge. To address this, this work proposed a distributed optical fiber vibration sensing system based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (Φ-OTDR) for drainage pipeline monitoring. To accurately capture abnormal events from complex environmental noise, a two-tier intelligent processing architecture comprising localization and classification modules was developed. The localization module employed an enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) model integrating anchor-box optimization, a channel-attention module, and an additional small-target feature layer, achieving a mean average precision of 96.8% in laboratory tests. The classification module utilized a hybrid model combining convolutional neural network, bidirectional long short-term memory, and attention classifier, achieving an overall accuracy of 98.1% for five abnormal events. During two-week of continuous field monitoring, the system localized simulated events with errors below 2.60 m and distinguished internal leakage, knocking, and drilling from walking, running, and vehicle interference with precision and recall exceeding 99.6% for the tested classes. Notably, the system successfully detected and accurately localized an actual branch pipe leakage event, demonstrating its practical effectiveness under real-world operating conditions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Chemically Stratified Urban Boundary Layer: Seasonally Reversing Vertical Changes in the Underlying Chemistry of Atmospheric Oxidation Capacity.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The vertical structure of atmospheric oxidation capacity (AOC) and its underlying radical chemistry within the urban boundary layer remains poorly characterized, yet it governs secondary pollutant formation. Here, we combined tower-based vertical observations with process-resolved model simulations in Beijing across winter and summer. We find that AOC generally declined with height in both seasons, but radical concentrations exhibit opposite vertical gradients. Notably, enhanced biogenic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emissions in summer suppress near-surface OH levels, creating a mid-altitude maximum. However, sharp vertical NO gradients drove an increase in ROx with height in winter. The underlying chemistry of vertical AOC variation shifts with the seasons. In winter, the photolysis of HONO dominates ROx production, and NOx-driven ROx loss prevails. In summer, the photolysis of oxygenated VOCs takes over, with radical self-reactions as the primary ROx sink. These findings demonstrate that surface observations alone may provide an incomplete representation of the whole boundary-layer chemistry.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Ionizing Radiation Sustains Fenton Oxidation through Radiolytic Fe Redox Cycling for Deep Mineralization of Refractory Pollutants.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The limited regeneration of Fe(II) from Fe(III) constrains sustained oxidation and mineralization in conventional Fenton processes. Here, we investigate an ionizing radiation-assisted Fenton process (IRFP) in which radiolytic Fe redox cycling sustains Fe-mediated oxidation. Using sulfasalazine as a model pollutant, we demonstrate that radiolytically generated hydrated electrons support two coupled pathways: rapid H2O2 activation and the conversion of Fe(III) to Fe(II). The resulting Fe redox cycling dynamically replenishes the Fe(II) pool alongside radiolytic H2O2 activation, thereby sustaining oxidative transformation beyond the initial degradation stage. Compared with irradiation and conventional Fenton treatment, IRFP promoted deeper fragmentation of azo, sulfonamide, and aromatic structures, resulting in enhanced mineralization. Transformation-product analysis further showed that continued transformation in IRFP reduced the persistence of complex intermediates with elevated predicted toxicity. In real pharmaceutical and coking wastewaters, IRFP achieved effective treatment under near-neutral conditions with substantially lower H2O2 and Fe(II) requirements than Fenton treatment and lower absorbed doses than irradiation alone. Although its electricity demand remained higher than short-time Fenton treatment, the markedly lower dosage of chemicals reduced the potential iron sludge burden and resulted in lower estimated COD-normalized treatment costs under the investigated conditions. These findings establish radiolytic Fe redox cycling as a strategy for sustaining Fe-mediated oxidation and promoting deeper transformation and mineralization of refractory pollutants.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Extracellular Polymeric Substances Govern Horizontal Gene Transfer of Antibiotic Resistance Genes: Mechanisms, Pathway Specificity, and Research Gaps.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The dissemination of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in environmental systems is recognized as being shaped by local matrix conditions, yet the pathway-specific role of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), the dominant matrix of biofilms, sludge flocs, and granules, remains poorly resolved. In this Review, we develop a mechanism- and pathway-resolved perspective for evaluating how EPS govern horizontal gene transfer (HGT) of ARGs. Current evidence indicates that conjugation is the most directly supported pathway, with EPS facilitating or restricting transfer through effects on donor-recipient contact, matrix organization, and transfer-related physiology. For transformation, EPS-associated extracellular ARGs constitute reservoirs, but EPS-DNA binding can both preserve genetic material and limit its immediate bioavailability. By contrast, EPS involvement in phage-mediated transduction and vesicle-mediated transfer remains mechanistically plausible but insufficiently validated. We identify five interconnected mechanisms: physical retention and spatial organization, DNA adsorption and bioavailability, regulation of intercellular contact, modulation of cell physiology and transfer competence, and community-scale mobilome coupling. By clarifying evidence boundaries across pathways, this Review moves EPS-HGT research from correlation-based interpretation toward mechanism-informed assessment of ARG mobility. We conclude by outlining research needs, including standardized EPS definition and extraction, component-resolved characterization, pathway-resolved causal assays, and validation in realistic environmental aggregates.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Dual Valorization of Mine Tailings for Critical Metal Extraction and Carbon Capture via Organic Acids.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The growing demand for critical elements (CEs) and carbon removal solutions creates opportunities to valorize mine waste. We investigate the organic acid-enhanced extraction of critical elements from wollastonite-rich tailings while assessing carbon dioxide (CO2) mineralization potential. Tailings were obtained from a mine in New York and contained aluminum, calcium, iron, magnesium, manganese, and titanium in wollastonite, pyroxene, garnet, and feldspar phases.
