Flow-through dissolution experiments at 40 and 80 °C using citric, formic, and oxalic acids (0.001-0.1 M), coupled with online pH, temperature, and pressure monitoring, were conducted, and the data were used to validate a multimineral kinetic model based on population balance equations, aqueous geochemistry, and ligand-dependent dissolution rate laws. Formic and oxalic acids achieved superior extraction, with formic acid particularly efficient for calcium─enabling coupled CEs recovery and CO2 mineralization. The ligand-promoted rate laws show a kinetic order of 0.5-1 with respect to formate activity for all minerals. Moreover, comparison of the estimated rates with previous works shows up to 1 order of magnitude faster dissolution in the presence of 0.1 M formic acid, reaching a plateau around pH 4 as the formate activity becomes constant. Overall, our multimineral kinetic framework demonstrates that model complexity should match element distribution, with mineral-specific kinetic models required for elements concentrated in distinct phases. In this way, the proposed approach provides a predictive tool to support sustainable tailings valorization.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Droplet-Shielded Micropore Raman-Activated Cell Sorting Improves Recovery of Emerging-Contaminant-Degrading Microorganisms.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Identifying, isolating, and cultivating functional microorganisms from complex environmental microbiomes remains a central challenge in linking microbial identity with contaminant transformation. Conventional Raman-activated cell sorting (RACS) enables label-free single-cell phenotyping but often compromises cell viability during laser interrogation and ejection, limiting the cultivation of functional indigenous microorganisms. Tire-wear-derived 6PPD-quinone (6PPDQ) is increasingly recognized as a highly toxic emerging contaminant in roadside soils, yet the indigenous microorganisms associated with its biological attenuation in roadside soils remain poorly characterized. Using 6PPDQ as a model emerging contaminant, we developed a droplet-shielded RACS platform based on a monolayer micropore-array chip that confines individual cells within picoliter-scale aqueous droplets during Raman phenotyping and laser ejection. Under the tested workflow-specific conditions, droplet-shielded RACS increased postsorting cultivation success of Escherichia coli from 13.9% to 95.6% and improved the cultivation success of 13C-6PPDQ-assimilating soil cells from 6.67% to 36.7%. Isotopic red shifts at 1001 and 1668 cm-1 enabled identification of cells assimilating 13C-6PPDQ-derived carbon. Guided by this strategy, we recovered indigenous 6PPDQ degraders affiliated with Bordetella and Brucella and confirmed their degradation capacity in pure culture. DNA-SIP provided complementary evidence for assimilation of 13C-labeled ring-derived carbon by the corresponding taxa. Single-cell genome amplification and sequencing identified cytochrome P450-, protocatechuate-, and catechol-metabolism-associated genes, indicating predicted metabolic potential in 6PPDQ transformation. Overall, droplet-shielded RACS provides a high-viability workflow for recovering contaminant-associated microorganisms from complex environmental microbiomes and enables their subsequent cultivation and functional characterization.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: High-Throughput Fingerprinting of Polymer Biodegradation across Phylogenetically Diverse Microorganisms.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: With the growing accumulation of plastic waste, focus has been directed toward biodegradable polymers; however, understanding their performance across diverse microbial communities requires species-level degradation data, which throughput-limited studies of undefined or limited consortia have only partially provided, preventing the cross-species and cross-polymer comparisons driving mechanistic understanding. This work presents an integrative framework fingerprinting polymer biodegradation across phylogenetically diverse microorganisms. A modified high-throughput clear-zone assay was adapted to physiologically diverse species through minimal media formulations and used to characterize fragmentation across 19 microorganisms and 14 commercial polymers. Paucimonas lemoignei, Priestia megaterium, and Pseudomonas stutzeri showed expansive fragmentation capability. Poly(1,4-butylene adipate), degraded by 11 of 19 species, proved most universally degradable, while poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate), poly(ε-caprolactone), and poly(lactic acid) were degraded more selectively. Plate-based screening of protease, esterase, and urease activity supported the aliphatic-ester selectivity pattern. MicroResp quantification, addressing the often-conflated distinction between fragmentation and mineralization, confirmed mineralization in 63.3% (19 of 30) fragmentation-positive pairs. Comparative genomics identified 465 depolymerase homologues, 187 with predicted signal peptides. Distinct strategies─P. lemoignei's four near-identical PhaZ paralogs versus P. stutzeri's divergent broad-substrate α/β hydrolases─explain their comparable polyester breadth. Overall, this framework establishes a foundation for systematic accumulation of microbial biodegradation fingerprints.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Patterns and Mitigation of Large Language Models' Hallucinations on Environmental Regulatory Facts.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: With increasing adoption of large language models (LLMs) in the environmental education, research, and policy domains, reducing hallucinations─where LLMs confidently produce wrong or fabricated results─remains a critical challenge toward trustworthy agentic AI. We evaluated hallucinations on 505 environmental water, air, and solids regulatory facts collected from U.S., China, the European Union (EU), and the World Health Organization (WHO). Across four open-weight and three commercial state-of-the-art LLMs evaluated in both English and Chinese, open-weight models hallucinated on 50-70% of facts, while commercial models hallucinated on only 7-15%. We discovered a deep geographic and linguistic imbalance, where LLMs hallucinate much less on U.S. facts, and when prompting in English. Although models were less confident on average when hallucinating, a non-trivial fraction of incorrect answers were still produced with high token-level confidence. Causal tracing identified layers where restoring the subject representation most strongly recovered correct answers, with patterns differing across models. Retrieval-augmented generation effectively mitigated hallucination, even for small open-weight models. Safe deployment of AI in high-stakes environmental workflows therefore requires both targeted mitigation of training biases and robust external knowledge grounding.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Enhanced CO2 Storage Capacity and Hydrate Formation Kinetics Using SDS-Stabilized CO2 Emulsions for Submarine Carbon Hydrate Storage.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Surfactant-assisted CO2 emulsion injection into cold aquifers offers enhanced CO2 storage capacity and accelerated hydrate formation. However, prior studies have largely treated surfactants as either emulsion stabilizers or hydrate kinetic promoters in isolation, leaving unresolved whether the concentration that optimizes CO2 trapping is compatible with that needed for hydrate formation near submarine temperatures. This study addresses that gap through a systematic, multiscale evaluation of SDS-stabilized CO2 emulsions. At ∼3 °C, SDS precipitates before reaching its critical micelle concentration; solubility, interfacial tension, and bulk hydrate formation experiments identify 1000 ppm as a practical upper limit for porous-medium experiments. High-pressure, low-temperature microfluidic experiments show that SDS above 500 ppm improves CO2-water displacement efficiency by increasing effective CO2-phase viscosity and reducing interfacial tension, yielding smaller CO2 ganglia and stable, piston-like displacement. SDS up to 1000 ppm shortens induction times and increases hydrate film growth rates, following a power-law dependence on subcooling with an exponent of 2. CO2 emulsions further sustain open transport pathways via continued CO2 dissolution, enabling efficient long-term CO2-to-hydrate conversion. These results define a concentration window where SDS simultaneously enhances CO2 storage and hydrate kinetics.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Prenatal Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and Body Mass Index Trajectories in Childhood: Application of Multiphase Growth Mixture Models across the ECHO Cohort.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: We examined the associations of prenatal per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposures with body mass index (BMI) trajectories and growth parameters in the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes Cohort. Maternal PFAS concentrations (perfluorohexanesulfonic acid [PFHxS], perfluorooctanesulfonic acid [PFOS], perfluorooctanoic acid [PFOA], perfluorononanoic acid [PFNA], perfluorodecanoic acid [PFDA], perfluoroundecanoic acid [PFUnDA], and N-methyl perfluorooctane sulfonamidoacetic acid [NMFOSAA]) were measured in serum or plasma during pregnancy. BMI trajectories and growth parameters were estimated using multiphase growth mixture modeling. Among 1,125 children ages 1-9.5 years, we identified a typical BMI trajectory (n = 998, 89%; reference group) and an atypical BMI trajectory characterized by early and rapid BMI increases (n = 127, 11%). Maternal PFOA (adjusted risk ratio [RR] = 1.22 per doubling; 95% CI = 1.05-1.41) and PFOS (adjusted RR = 1.14; 95% CI = 0.99-1.32) concentrations were associated with a higher risk of atypical trajectory membership. A doubling in maternal PFOA concentrations was associated with an earlier age at adiposity rebound by 19 (95% CI = 4-33) days. Other PFAS concentrations were not significantly associated with the atypical trajectory or adiposity rebound. In this pooled cohort study, higher prenatal exposure to certain PFAS was associated with a greater risk of an obesity-related growth trajectory and earlier adiposity rebound.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Interaction Between Siderite and Goethite Regulates Fe(II) Speciation and Sustains Reduction Capacity.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Fe(II) drives many reduction reactions in aquifers, and its reactivity is governed not merely by total abundance but also by its speciation. Siderite is a major reservoir of structural Fe(II) and frequently occurs in close proximity with goethite. But whether such close proximity effects transformation of structural Fe(II) remains unclear. This study demonstrated that coupling siderite dissolution and diffusive transport established a narrow microenvironment between siderite surface and bulk solutions, which has higher aqueous Fe(II) (Fe(II)aq) concentration and increased pH. Close proximity enables goethite to access the microenvironment and form the proton-mediated feedback interaction with siderite, promoting the formation of surface-associated Fe(II). Therefore, the surface-associated Fe(II) pool in mixed systems increased to 109.3-538.7 μM, 2.8-13.7 times higher than that in dual-chamber systems. This increase can be quantitatively predicted from siderite surface area (A) and proton activity (aH+) via a unified relationship (A·aH+0.37). The A determines the number of available reaction sites, and the aH+ governs the reaction rate. Nitrobenzene reduction experiments revealed that surface-associated Fe(II) pool sustained reduction capacity over successive reaction cycles by linking structural Fe(II) and Fe(II)aq. These findings identify interaction between siderite and goethite as an overlooked mechanism for generating a persistent surface-associated Fe(II) pool. The species distribution of Fe(II) determines the durability of abiotic natural attenuation in aquifers.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: A Supervised and Visualization-Enabled Toolkit for Robust DNA Reference Database Construction in eDNA Biomonitoring.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) and DNA-based technologies are increasingly used for biodiversity assessment, but their taxonomic resolution depends strongly on the quality, completeness, and interoperability of reference databases. Public barcode repositories often contain heterogeneous sequence lengths, inconsistent taxonomy, redundant records, and incomplete metadata, and existing tools do not always provide supervised curation, visual inspection, controlled database extension, and multiformat export in one workflow. Here, we present MFRefData (Multi-Format Reference Database), a Python-based toolkit for constructing customized reference databases using a paired CSV-FASTA architecture. MFRefData integrates NCBI sequence retrieval, primer-specific in silico PCR, standardized taxonomic annotation, VSEARCH-based dereplication, rule-based filtering, controlled database extension, visualization, and export to multiple commonly used compatible formats. Using the Pearl River fishes under standardized input conditions, MFRefData retrieved more sequences and covered more species than the refdb and CRABS toolkits, while also achieving higher sequence retrieval efficiency and memory efficiency. In an in silico mock community of 40 fish species and three mitochondrial 12S primer sets, MFRefData produced more correct species-level assignments than databases generated by the refdb and CRABS toolkits. Applied to real eDNA samples, MFRefData recovered broader species-level biodiversity signals. Overall, MFRefData provides a supervised, visualization-enabled, and multiformat framework for improving reference database transparency, technical quality control, and reproducibility, while supporting more reliable species-level taxonomic assignments in DNA-based biodiversity assessment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Harvesting Corrosion Energy for Self-Powered Gravity-Driven Membrane Filtration and Fouling Regulation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Decentralized water treatment requires low-cost technologies that can remove dissolved metal ions while maintaining stable water production without external energy input. Here, we developed a soil-mediated corrosion-current hydrogel filtration system (SCHFs) that integrates a conductive adsorptive hydrogel membrane with a soil-based corrosion-energy-harvesting unit. Natural soil served as the solid electrolyte, while discarded Al and carbon cloth enabled direct harvesting of corrosion energy for conductive-membrane regulation during gravity-driven filtration. In 60-day continuous river water filtration, the SCHFs permeate concentrations of Cu2+ and Mn2+ approaching the detection limit under the tested conditions. In addition, SCHFs also accelerated NH4+-N stabilization and reduced the final permeate concentration to 0.2 mg L-1. Moreover, a thicker but more porous surface cake layer was formed during SCHF operation, limiting pore blockage and reducing the 60-day flux decline. Microbial community analysis further indicated that SCHFs reshaped the membrane biofilm and enriched taxa associated with nitrogen transformation. Soil and electrode analyses suggested that Al released from the sacrificial electrode was partly immobilized as aluminum-containing silicate minerals, suggesting a low secondary environmental risk under controlled Al input. These results suggest that coupling soil-mediated microcurrent in SCHFs regulate interfacial transport and fouling-layer architecture, thereby improving dissolved-metal retention and long-term hydraulic stability.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Electrochemical Recycling of Spent Lithium-Ion Battery Cathodes: Direct Regeneration, Electrochemical Leaching, and Selective Separation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Growing volumes of spent lithium-ion batteries challenge waste management and resource security. Conventional recycling recovers metals but often consumes energy and chemicals while sacrificing cathode structural value. Electrochemical methods enable cathode repair, controlled dissolution, and selective recovery, yet their suitability for diverse feeds and product requirements remains unclear. This Critical Review develops a material-state- and product-oriented framework linking cathode degradation, electrochemical transformations, and product specifications. Relithiation, defect repair, and cell-level rejuvenation are evaluated as regeneration strategies, with functional repurposing considered separately. Electrochemical leaching is classified by direct or indirect redox transfer, while paired or coupled operation is treated as reactor-level integration. Electrodialysis, electrosorption, and electrodeposition are assessed for ion redistribution, selective capture, concentration, and product formation. Because extraction efficiency alone cannot establish successful recycling, we emphasize feedstock tolerance, selectivity, Faradaic and ion-transport efficiencies, energy and reagent consumption, component durability, and qualified-product yield within defined system boundaries. Future priorities include diagnosis-guided routing, realistic black-mass validation, standardized reporting, scalable reactors, and integrated techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Electrochemical technologies can complement established recycling through feedstock-adaptive pathways that retain, recover, or upgrade cathode value.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Multiomics: TBPH Enhances Thyroid Hormone Synthesis via PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 Pathway.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Bis(2-ethylhexyl)-tetrabromophthalate (TBPH), a high-production-volume novel brominated flame retardant (NBFR), has been shown to perturb thyroid hormone synthesis, yet the underlying molecular mechanism remains poorly understood. Using transcriptomics, phosphoproteomics, and metabolomics as discovery tools, combined with validation in Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats and human thyroid follicular epithelial cells (Nthy-ori 3-1), we investigated this mechanism. TBPH increased thyroglobulin (TG) and thyroid peroxidase (TPO) in rat thyroid and elevated circulating triiodothyronine (T3) and thyroxine (T4) levels. In Nthy-ori 3-1 cells, TBPH remodeled glycerophospholipid metabolism, leading to phosphatidylinositol synthase (PIS)-dependent accumulation of the signaling lipid lysophosphatidylinositol 18:1 (LPI_18:1). LPI 18:1 selectively activated the ERK-EGR1 signaling axis and drove TG/TPO upregulation. Knockdown of PIS or EGR1, or pharmacological inhibition of ERK, abolished TBPH-induced TG/TPO expression. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized PIS-LPI-ERK-EGR1 pathway through which TBPH enhances thyroid hormone synthesis, highlighting a lipid metabolism-driven mechanism of endocrine disruption and providing a mechanistic basis for reassessing the health risks of NBFRs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Dual Regulation of Monomer Transport Enables Ultrahigh Mg2+/Li+ Selectivity in Polyamide Nanofiltration Membranes.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nanofiltration membranes are promising for lithium recovery from salt-lake brines, yet their Mg2+/Li+ separation performance can be further improved. Here, we present an organic-phase engineering strategy that systematically tailors the carbon-chain length of alkane solvents, from n-hexane (C6) to 2-methylundecane (C12), to simultaneously regulate piperazine enrichment at the water-organic interface and trimesoyl chloride diffusion kinetics. This dual regulation transforms conventional rapid and random interfacial polymerization into a more confined and homogeneous growth process. The resulting polyamide membranes exhibit a reduced negative surface charge and a narrower and more uniform pore-size distribution. These structural features substantially enhance Mg2+/Li+ separation, with the C12 membrane achieving a Mg2+/Li+ selectivity of up to 306.6 in the mixed-salt solutions. To assess performance under realistic conditions, a two-pass nanofiltration process was evaluated using simulated salt-lake brine. The C12 membrane increased lithium purity from 2.4% to 97.7% while reducing the Mg2+/Li+ mass ratio from 40 to 0.024. This study provides new insight into the kinetic regulation of interfacial polymerization through organic-phase engineering and demonstrates an effective membrane design strategy for high-selectivity lithium extraction from complex brines.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Novel Multi-Isotope Am and Cm Signatures Trace Temporal Changes in Nuclear Inputs in a Baltic Sediment Core.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Anthropogenic radionuclides have been present in the environment since 1945 due to civil and military uses of nuclear energy. This study represents an extensive characterization of Am and Cm isotopes (241Am, 242mAm, 243Am, 244Cm, 245Cm, 246Cm), and 237Np, in a Baltic Sea sediment core directly impacted by discharges from the Studsvik nuclear research facility (Sweden). Distinct isotopic signatures were identified throughout the sediment core, enabling discrimination between inputs from atmospheric nuclear weapons testing (1952-1965), Sweden's nuclear-weapons-related activities during the 1970s, and subsequent releases associated with civil nuclear-energy development. The findings demonstrate that higher actinides provide powerful isotopic fingerprints for resolving complex nuclear contamination histories and attributing release sources in environmental archives. This study further establishes the utility of actinide isotopic tracers beyond U and Pu and presents the first environmental application of the 243Am/241Am ratio in a system with well-constrained inputs from distinct nuclear sources.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Microbial Influence on Corrosive Processes at the Cast Iron-Bentonite Interface during 3.5 Years of Incubation at 37 and 70 °C.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Bentonite-based geotechnical barriers constitute currently an integral part of international disposal concepts of high-level radioactive waste in claystone and crystalline rock. Elevated temperature, canister corrosion, and metabolic activity of microorganisms can influence their performance. To study these effects on processes at the cast iron-bentonite interface, microcosms were incubated with two different bentonites (B27 and GMZ-001), synthetic Opalinus Clay pore water with a high water-to-bentonite ratio and cast iron plates at 37 and 70 °C over a period of 3.5 years. No microorganisms or nutrients were added to those naturally occurring in the applied materials. Cast iron surfaces in contact with GMZ-001 bentonite appeared strongly corroded, and secondary layer-like structures formed at both temperatures. Furthermore, an accelerated release of iron into the pore water, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up were observed. In contrast, incubation with B27 bentonite at 37 °C resulted in less corroded cast iron surfaces covered with iron sulfides, which seemed to passivate the surface and led to lower iron release, H2 generation, and gas pressure build-up. Respective B27 microcosms were dominated by metabolically active sulfate-reducing bacteria that induced iron sulfide formation. This study shows that the corrosion behavior of cast iron and changes in geochemical parameters like pH and pore water composition depend on the applied bentonite, naturally occurring microorganisms, and temperature.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Occurrence and Environmental Weathering of Agricultural Microplastics on Beaches across Japan: Insights into Surface Mineralization and Metal Binding.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: We investigated the coastal occurrence and environmental weathering of microplastics derived from polymer-coated fertilizers (PCFs) across Japan. A field survey along the Japanese coastline revealed that PCF-derived microplastics are widely distributed on beaches throughout the country, indicating that agricultural microplastics have dispersed far beyond agricultural landscapes. Compositional analysis showed that these particles consist predominantly of polyolefins (∼70%) and polyurethanes (∼30%) and commonly exhibit oxidative degradation accompanied by iron enrichment. Bulk elemental analysis demonstrated positive correlations between iron and multiple heavy metals. Micro-X-ray fluorescence mapping using a focused 20-μm beam showed that chromium is heterogeneously distributed on the plastic surface and spatially associated with iron, while X-ray absorption spectroscopy indicated its occurrence in ferrihydrite-like phases or as chromite. Although detailed spectroscopic evidence was obtained from a single selected particle, the widespread occurrence of PCF-derived microplastics and their observed metal enrichment suggest that similar geochemical processes may occur at other coastal sites. By linking nationwide field observations with process-level characterization, this study shows that microplastics have the potential to transition from inert debris to geochemically reactive substrates after coastal deposition.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Metatranscriptomics Reveals Potential Hybrid Electron Routing in Comammox Nitrospira and NO-Supplemented Cooperation in a Partial Nitritation-Anammox Bioreactor under Dynamic Aeration.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Intermittent aeration drives partial nitritation-anammox (PN-A) systems, yet how microbiomes regulate aerobic and anaerobic respiration during rapid, oxygen-limited redox shifts remains poorly understood. Here, we applied genome-resolved metatranscriptomics to evaluate transcriptional dynamics in a long-term PN-A bioreactor treating low concentrations of ammonium. Under intermittent aeration, active populations did not follow strict metabolic switching, but instead exhibited complementary regulation by coordinately transcribing aerobic and anaerobic respiratory pathways. Notably, comammox Nitrospira exhibited a severe transcriptional bottleneck, with terminal oxidase expression 2-3 orders of magnitude lower than that of amo and nirK. Gene coexpression and pathway mapping support a novel hybrid electron transport chain where electrons from ammonia oxidation are directly routed to nirK. This alternative electron-transfer route functionally couples energy dissipation with obligatory nitrite detoxification. Concurrently, a severe transcriptional deficit of nirS relative to hdh in anammox Ca. Kuenenia indicates a partial bypass of intracellular nitrite reduction. Collectively, these patterns support a novel nitric oxide-supplemented cooperation: anammox bacteria scavenge extracellular nitric oxide generated by comammox Nitrospira, conserving their own electrons while acting as a vital sink to relieve comammox nitric oxide toxicity. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for optimizing advanced PN-A microbiomes through engineered aeration control.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Discovery of Emerging Aromatic Compounds with High Potential Risk from Coal-Fired Power Plants.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Coal combustion releases aromatic compound (AC) mixtures far more complex than the 16 EPA-priority polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). Here, a high-resolution in-house database targeting 104 aromatic compounds prioritized by structural carcinogenicity alerts and structural analogy was developed to complement NIST library matching for screening fly ash, slag, and soil from five coal-fired power plants (CFPPs). This dual-database strategy increased the identification rate by 9.2% and captured 29 compounds previously unreported in the analyzed CFPP-related matrices. A total of 393 ACs spanning 24 structural classes were annotated. Cross-matrix profiling revealed distinct chemical shifts, from primary 1-ring products in slag to secondary chlorinated species in fly ash and ultimately to persistent high-molecular-weight PAHs in soils, suggesting that the observed AC patterns were associated with differences in unit efficiency, end-of-pipe control, and operational history across the five CFPPs. Incremental lifetime cancer risk assessment demonstrated that emerging PAHs contributed 60% of the total carcinogenic risk in fly ash despite comprising only ∼2% of total AC concentrations, with 4-ring compounds identified as the predominant risk drivers. Sensitivity analysis confirmed that assessments restricted to literature-derived toxic equivalency factors underestimate the full carcinogenic potential. These findings reveal a critical yet underrecognized toxic fraction in CFPP fly ash, underscoring the need for risk-oriented management strategies that explicitly incorporate emerging PAHs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Context-Aware Multitask Learning for Aquatic and Soil Ecotoxicity Prediction from Fragmented ECOTOX Records.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Large ecotoxicity databases contain extensive evidence, yet heterogeneous reporting and sparse coverage across chemicals, species, end points, and conditions limit predictive use. From relational U.S. EPA ECOTOX, we linked 1,234,077 traceable records and constructed model-ready aquatic and soil data sets of 219,818 and 11,532 records. We developed a context-aware multitask model that preserves end point-specific responses while sharing information across molecular, biological, and experimental contexts. On held-out condition keys and parent-species-task combinations, four-seed ensembles achieved pooled R2 of 0.758/0.751 for aquatic toxicity and 0.628/0.537 for soil toxicity. Compared with same-input single-task models, multitask fitting reduced soil task-macro mean absolute error (MAE) by 0.136/0.156 across 16 task heads; aquatic point estimates also favored sharing, although uncertainty across all aquatic task heads was not estimable. Under canonical-parent holdout, frozen shared representations reduced task-macro MAE by 0.170-0.180 in aquatic and 0.093-0.125 in soil tree models versus molecular-only inputs, indicating reusable predictive information. Multidimensional training support stratified parent-holdout errors, meeting prespecified criteria fully for soil and partially for aquatic predictions; benefits weakened under stronger structural separation. These results show model-ready ECOTOX data can support context-aware toxicity prediction across a sparse experimental matrix, helping prioritize informative measurements and providing a predictive evidence base for environmental hazard assessment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Warming Patterns Shape Divergent Multilevel Physiological Responses and Underlying Metabolic Mechanisms in Aquatic Organisms.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Although the impacts of global warming on aquatic ecosystems are widely recognized, the biological consequences of distinct warming patterns remain largely unknown. We investigated physiological and metabolic responses of Daphnia magna, Chironomus kiiensis, and zebrafish under constant warming (+1, +3 °C), heatwave, and temperature fluctuation. Dynamic patterns exhibited stronger physiological responses, with mean absolute effect sizes across survival, growth, development, behavior, and stress functional categories following the order heatwave > fluctuation > +3 °C > +1 °C. Response profiles varied among warming patterns: constant +3 °C induced moderate and broad changes across biochemical stress, developmental, and behavioral end points; heatwave accelerated zebrafish hatching and C. kiiensis pupation while increasing deformity, suppressing growth, and elevating mortality; and fluctuation induced pronounced biochemical stress responses, particularly HSP70, together with developmental disruption, while producing weaker survival and growth effects than heatwave. Across taxa, dominant response profiles differed, with broad multiend point disruption in D. magna, stress-dominant responses in C. kiiensis, and developmental sensitivity in zebrafish. Metabolomic analysis further identified warming-pattern-specific metabolic signatures associated with energy metabolism under +3 °C, membrane-related processes under heatwave, and redox-related processes under fluctuation. Together, these findings provide a scientific basis for improving aquatic ecological risk assessment under increasingly variable warming scenarios.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Nanoplastic Size Governs the Decoupling of Microbial Survival from Antibiotic Degradation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics co-occur in wastewater systems, but how NP size influences antibiotic biodegradation by specialized degraders remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of europium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; PS20 and PS100) on sulfadiazine biodegradation by Arthrobacter sp. strain D2. Modified Gompertz modeling revealed two contrasting inhibition regimes. For PS100, inhibition was dominated by lag-phase prolongation, with no detectable sulfadiazine removal over 48 h at a PS100 concentration of 100 mg L-1. In contrast, PS20 reduced the maximum sulfadiazine degradation rate by ∼40% while causing only minor changes in lag time, indicating rate-dominated inhibition. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring at a model sulfadiazine-enriched interface showed that PS100 markedly reduced the deposition of NP-pre-exposed cells, whereas PS20 only partially impaired adhesion. Transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further revealed intracellular accumulation of PS20, whereas PS100 remained predominantly extracellular. Phase-specific physiological measurements and transcriptomics suggested that PS20 induced oxidative-stress responses associated with reduced sulfadiazine biodegradation rates, whereas PS100 elicited dose-dependent transcriptional changes during lag-phase extension. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoplastics impair antibiotic attenuation through distinct size-dependent mechanisms involving interface-associated constraints and intracellular interference, highlighting particle size as a key determinant of antibiotic fate in plastic-contaminated wastewater environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Unveiling Whole Water Neurotoxicity through Sensitive Electrophysiological Functional Profiling: Beyond Conventional Morphological Metrics.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Neuroactive contaminants typically coexist as complex mixtures in aquatic ecosystems, exerting deleterious effects through combined exposures. However, current assessment approaches based on morphological endpoints (e.g., neurite outgrowth) lack sufficient sensitivity to capture functional neurotoxicity of these mixtures. To address this gap, this study establishes in vitro functional neurotoxicity testing (iFNT), an ultrasensitive bioassay leveraging high-density microelectrode arrays to profile cortical network electrophysiology. Validated using reference toxicants, their mixture, and whole water samples, iFNT achieves 5- to 500-fold higher sensitivity than the neurite outgrowth assay. This heightened sensitivity enables clearer discrimination of functional phenotypes for both individual compounds at environmentally relevant concentrations (10-8 M) and whole water samples without preconcentration, providing a powerful tool for evaluating real-world neurotoxic risks. Alarmingly, conventional monitoring indicators exhibited a pronounced mismatch with iFNT profiles across wastewater treatment stages, demonstrating that seemingly acceptable routine readings masked the persistence of latent neurotoxicity. This study challenges morphology-based paradigms, revealing that accurate whole water risk assessment necessitates integrating functional biological endpoints into future monitoring frameworks.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Microbial Degradation of Lignin Generates Iron-Binding Organic Ligands.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The association of organic carbon (OC) with iron (Fe) minerals is a primary mechanism governing soil OC persistence, yet the molecular agents mediating Fe-OC binding remain poorly defined. In this study, we demonstrated that microbial degradation of lignin, one of the major contributors to soil OC, generates organic compounds with the potential to bind to Fe, with implications for mineral-associated carbon stabilization. Lignin samples were microbially degraded by Pseudomonas putida KT2440 for 30 days and subsequently reacted with FeCl3. Ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography-high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC-HRMS/MS)-based analysis identified 494 distinct molecular features with MS/MS data, of which 21 were identified as lignin-derived Fe-binding ligands using Fe isotopologue-enabled metabolomics. Structural annotation of 15 identified ligands further elucidated the chemical nature of the lignin-derived compounds. Systematic meta-analysis of more than 20,000 public HRMS datasets revealed that related compounds occur in soil and aquatic organic matter across diverse ecosystems, ranging from grassland to Arctic tundra. Ion identity molecular networking (IIMN) further revealed additional putative ligands and structurally related transformation products. Altogether, our findings provide a molecular framework for investigating how microbially generated Fe-binding ligands may contribute to Fe-OC interactions and potentially, soil carbon stabilization under changing climate conditions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Data-Driven Accelerated Design-Synthesis of Heterogeneous Fenton-like Catalysts for Water Decontamination.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysis offers an effective approach for organic pollutant removal, yet catalyst development remains largely empirical and lacks a closed-loop design-synthesis-validation framework. Here, we report a synthesis-oriented inverse-design framework for Fe-based catalysts. We first developed ML_Removal to predict pollutant removal, achieving a test-set R2 of 0.970, while SHAP analysis identified specific surface area (SSA) and Fe loading (Fe wt %) as actionable catalyst descriptors. We then built two synthesis-to-property models to predict SSA and Fe wt %, with SMOTER augmentation enhancing model performance and yielding test-set R2 of 0.782 and 0.856, respectively. Coupling these models with NSGA-II enabled the identification of candidate synthesis recipes targeting the SSA and Fe wt % windows. Two catalysts synthesized according to the NSGA-II-derived recipes exhibited measured SSA of 538.40 and 468.63 m2/g and Fe wt % of 8.19 and 7.01 wt %, aligning with the design targets. The catalysts achieved broad pollutant removal, retained activity in real waters matrices, and maintained >71% naproxen removal after five cycles. External validation of ML_Removal using the experimental data sets yielded an R2 of 0.784, demonstrating transferability to pollutants absent from the training set. Overall, this work establishes a closed-loop design-synthesis-validation framework for data-driven catalyst development and experimental realization.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Lattice-Oxygen-Mediated Electronic Reconstruction of High-Entropy Oxides for Durable Fenton-like Water Treatment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: High-entropy catalysts offer broad compositional tunability for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based water treatment, yet achieving rapid, selective, and durable oxidation remains challenging because metallic bonding in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) limits electronic communication among metal sites. Here, we construct a quinary high-entropy oxide (HEO, (FeCoNiMnCu)3O4) featuring an oxygen-bridged M-O-M framework that enables local electronic coupling among neighboring metal centers. X-ray absorption spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support oxygen-mediated charge redistribution, with Hirshfeld analysis indicating 0.46e of charge transfer toward adsorbed PMS. Temperature-dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a substantially lower apparent activation energy for interfacial charge transfer in the HEO (0.43 eV) than in the HEA (1.15 eV). Mechanistic experiments support a predominantly nonradical PMS activation pathway involving high-valent cobalt-oxo species and singlet oxygen. The HEO achieved near-complete phenol degradation and 87.9% total organic carbon removal within 10 min, with an apparent rate constant of 0.359 min-1 versus 0.113 min-1 for the HEA. The system maintained >90% phenol removal across pH 3-11, sustained activity over 30 reuse cycles, and retained effective contaminant removal during continuous-flow operation and 50 L bench-scale treatment. These results support lattice-oxygen-mediated electronic reconstruction as a strategy for coupling efficient PMS activation with structural durability in high-entropy oxide catalysts.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Synthetic DNA Tracers Enable Ultra-High-Reproducibility Characterization of Aquifer Hydraulic Conductivity and Contaminant Transport.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Reliable characterization of aquifer hydraulic conductivity (K) via tracer-based methods remains a major challenge due to environmental background noise. We report that synthetic DNA tracers, free of background-noise interference, enable highly reproducible tomographic inversion of K fields across six replicate experiments conducted in a heterogeneous laboratory sandbox measuring 180 cm (length) × 10 cm (width) × 90 cm (height) at a steady flow rate of approximately 177.4 cm3 min-1. The results demonstrate superior reproducibility of the DNA tracers relative to dye tracers across three evaluation levels: travel-time consistency, where the contrast is most pronounced (mean R2 = 0.84 for DNA tracers versus R2 = 0.10 for dye tracers), inverted lnK field coherence, and prediction-level robustness. Contaminant-transport forecasts under four scenarios, spanning pulse versus continuous releases and conservative versus decaying solutes, further indicate that DNA-derived K fields yield substantially more stable predictions than dye-derived K fields in nearly all cases. These advantages arise from the standardized molecular design of oligonucleotides and their sequence-specific quantitation via qPCR, which collectively mitigate background interference and tracer-specific transport artifacts. These findings show that synthetic DNA tracers constitute a promising tool for aquifer characterization, addressing a critical gap in tracer-based tomography for groundwater investigations.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Far-UVC Activation of Performic Acid Enables Concurrent Oxidative and Reductive Micropollutant Abatement.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Conventional UV-driven advanced oxidation and reduction processes generally emphasize one redox regime and can be inhibited by wastewater constituents. Here, we characterize the photochemistry of performic acid (PFA) under 222 and 254 nm irradiation and evaluate the capacity of PFA solution, prepared from H2O2 and formic acid and thus containing residual H2O2 and formate, to generate concurrent oxidative and reductive pathways. Relative to 254 nm, 222 nm irradiation increased the fluence-normalized photodecay rate constants of neutral PFA (PFA0) and its conjugate base (PFA-) by 1.21- and 3.81-fold, respectively. The increase arose from 16.1- and 10.1-fold larger molar absorption coefficients at 222 nm, despite lower fitted innate quantum yields (0.367 and 0.804 molecule photon-1 at 222 nm versus 0.587 and 0.819 molecule photon-1 at 254 nm). The UV222/PFA solution system generated the reductant •CO2- together with oxidative HO• and oxygen-centered organic radicals. Pathway analysis attributed 34% of carbamazepine removal to •CO2- and 19% of naproxen removal to R-O• at 222 nm. Chloride and bromide enhanced fluence-normalized degradation through reactive-halogen chemistry; the largest increases were observed for carbamazepine (47.5-fold at 254 nm and 21.9-fold at 222 nm). In real municipal wastewater, UV222/PFA solution decreased total organic carbon by 33.5% within 60 min, compared with 21.6% under UV254/PFA solution, at an initial PFA concentration of 80 μM. These results suggest far-UVC activation of PFA solution as a dual-redox treatment platform, with the observed advantages maintained in the tested wastewater effluents.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Basalt Application Alters the Nitrogen Budget of Midwestern U.S. Agricultural Soils through Reduced Nitrous Oxide Fluxes and Increased Nitrogen Leaching.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Land-based enhanced rock weathering (ERW)─applying ground silicate rock to soils─is being explored for sequestration of CO2 from the atmosphere, with impacts beyond carbon storage. Weathering of basalt releases base cations increasing alkalinity and soil pH, which we hypothesized would reduce N2O emissions. Repeated applications of basalt to a heavily fertilized annual Zea mays and Glycine max rotation (maize and soybean) and the low-fertilized perennial bioenergy grass Miscanthus x giganteus (miscanthus) in Illinois raised soil pH from 6.6 to 7.1 in maize/soybean and from 5.4 to 6.3 in miscanthus and consistently reduced annual N2O emissions by 16-40% over 7 growing seasons. Although not statistically significant for any given crop, our results indicate an emerging trend of increased N leaching (23% pooled across crops and years), suggesting a potential shift in N loss from the atmosphere to groundwater. Crop yields increased or remained unchanged, indicating enhanced weathering is compatible with conventional farming practices. Regional land model simulations show that ERW deployment across the US Corn Belt could reduce soil N2O emissions by 11% under a moderate deployment pathway and by 24% under a more intensive deployment pathway. The effects of enhanced weathering extend beyond CO2 sequestration and may benefit both greenhouse gas mitigation and bioenergy crop production, with a potential trade-off of increased N mobility in fertile, organic matter-rich US Midwestern soils.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Convergent Biogenic Magnetite Formation from Diverse Iron (Oxyhydr)oxide Precursors Drives Cr(VI) Reduction via an Environmental Battery Mechanism.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Iron (oxyhydr)oxides mediate electron flux across coupled biogeochemical cycles in anoxic environments, yet whether their biogenic transformation feeds back to reshape interfacial electron transfer efficiency remains unresolved. Here, five structurally distinct iron (oxyhydr)oxide precursors (ferrihydrite, goethite, magnetite, wüstite, and hematite) were exposed to anaerobic sulfur-oxidizing bioreactors under Cr(VI) stress, and their transformation trajectories were tracked using synchrotron EXAFS spectroscopy, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, DFT calculations, and metagenomic profiling. Mineral bioavailability decreased in the order ferrihydrite > goethite > magnetite > wüstite > hematite, a hierarchy governed by lattice iron-leaching energetics quantified via DFT (Efev from -8.96 eV for ferrihydrite to 5.76 eV for hematite). Despite this wide disparity in precursor lability, all biotransformation trajectories converged on magnetite as the thermodynamically stable end point. In the ferrihydrite system, biogenic magnetite reached 60% of the final solid phase and operated as an in situ "environmental battery" (storing and releasing electrons through reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) lattice cycling), lowering interfacial charge transfer resistance and producing a 4.77-fold higher pseudo-first-order Cr(VI) reduction rate constant than the mineral-free biotic control (C-S). Metagenomic analysis revealed mineral-specific restructuring of the microbial community toward a tightly coupled sulfur-iron redox network. These results reframe precursor mineralogy from a determinant of intrinsic reactivity to a kinetic regulator of biogenic electron-buffer formation, providing a mechanistic basis for mineral-informed bioremediation design.
